messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide that shows you how to **generate** and **execute** a RESTful request for the “Get information of device connector versions” API on Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. The instructions assume you already have a Nexus Dashboard instance running and that you have the necessary credentials (username/password or OAuth client) to authenticate. --- ## 1. Find the API in the Dashboard UI | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **1.1** | Log in to the Nexus Dashboard web UI (HTTPS). | You need a session to access the API Explorer. | | **1.2** | From the left‑hand navigation, click **Developer Tools** → **API Explorer**. | The API Explorer is the built‑in tool that lets you discover, test, and generate requests for all exposed APIs. | | **1.3** | In the search box, type **“device connector versions”** or simply **“device‑connector‑versions”**. | This filters the list to the relevant API. | | **1.4** | Click the API entry that reads **“Get information of device connector versions”**. | Opens the detailed view of the endpoint. | > **Tip:** If you’re not sure of the exact name, you can also browse the **“Device Connector”** section of the API Explorer; the endpoint will be listed there. --- ## 2. Inspect the API details When you open the API, you’ll see: | Section | What you’ll see | How to use it | |---------|-----------------|---------------| | **Method** | `GET` | The HTTP verb you’ll use. | | **Path** | `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` | The relative URL you’ll hit. | | **Query Parameters** | e.g. `deviceConnectorId`, `page`, `size` | Optional filters; you can leave them blank if you want all versions. | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | Required for authentication and content negotiation. | | **Response** | JSON schema | Shows the structure of the returned data. | --- ## 3. Generate the request | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **3.1** | In the API detail view, click the **“Generate Request”** button (usually located near the top right). | This copies a ready‑to‑use request to your clipboard. | | **3.2** | Paste the request into a text editor or directly into a terminal/curl command. | You’ll see something like: ``` GET /api/v1/device-connector/versions HTTP/1.1 Host: Authorization: Bearer Accept: application/json ``` | **3.3** | Replace `` with your actual host (e.g., `nexus-dashboard.company.com`). | The host must match your deployment. | | **3.4** | Replace `` with a valid bearer token. | Authentication is mandatory. | --- ## 4. Obtain a bearer token If you don’t already have a token, you can get one via the **Login** API or by using the UI’s “Get Token” button. ### Using the Login API ```bash curl -X POST \ https:///api/v1/auth/login \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "username": "your_user", "password": "your_password" }' ``` The response will contain a JSON object with a `token` field. Copy that value. > **Note:** Some deployments use OAuth2 client credentials; in that case, call `/api/v1/auth/token` with your client ID/secret. --- ## 5. Execute the request (cURL example) ```bash curl -X GET \ https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` **Optional query parameters** ```bash curl -X GET \ "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions?deviceConnectorId=12345&page=0&size=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` --- ## 6. Verify the response A successful call returns HTTP `200 OK` with JSON similar to: ```json { "total": 3, "page": 0, "size": 50, "versions": [ { "id": "v1.0.0", "releaseDate": "2023-01-15T00:00:00Z", "description": "Initial release" }, { "id": "v1.1.0", "releaseDate": "2023-04-20T00:00:00Z", "description": "Bug fixes and performance improvements" }, { "id": "v1.2.0", "releaseDate": "2023-07-10T00:00:00Z", "description": "New features added" } ] } ``` If you receive `401 Unauthorized`, double‑check the token and its expiration. If you receive `400 Bad Request`, verify that any required query parameters are correctly formatted. --- ## 7. Using Postman (optional) 1. Open Postman. 2. Create a new **GET** request. 3. Set the URL to `https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions`. 4. Under **Headers**, add: * `Authorization: Bearer ` * `Accept: application/json` 5. Click **Send**. 6. Inspect the response in the Postman UI. --- ## 8. Quick reference (cURL template) ```bash # 1. Get a token TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST \ https:///api/v1/auth/login \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"username":"your_user","password":"your_password"}' | jq -r .token) # 2. Call the API curl -X GET \ https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` *(Requires `jq` for JSON parsing; otherwise, manually copy the token.)* --- ## 9. Common pitfalls | Issue | Cause | Fix | |-------|-------|-----| | `401 Unauthorized` | Token expired or wrong | Re‑authenticate or refresh token | | `404 Not Found` | Wrong path or host | Verify the host and endpoint path | | `400 Bad Request` | Missing required query param | Add `deviceConnectorId` or other required params | | `500 Internal Server Error` | Backend issue | Check Nexus Dashboard logs or contact support | --- ### TL;DR 1. **Open API Explorer** → find “Get information of device connector versions”. 2. **Click “Generate Request”** → copy the request. 3. **Replace placeholders** (``, ``). 4. **Execute** via cURL/Postman. That’s all you need to generate and run the RESTful request for device connector versions on Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. Happy API‑calling!
